notes: 'Mark well' heads on the verb: 'well' is an intensifier, not a complement carrying the lexeme, and rule 31's subtraction leaves the lexeme with 'Mark'.

'Hold thy peace' is kept whole as the verb's idiomatic rendering, including the 'thy' the English formula requires (rule 30's closing sentence on formula pronouns); rule 18's supplied-possessive clause does not reach a possessive inside a fixed rendering of a verb.
The subject pronoun of the last clause belongs to the explicit ʾānōkî, so the verb keeps only 'will speak'.
